active_goal: comprehensive compressed image codec generation support

policy_decisions.recommendation: Prefer project-owned Rust adapters or pinned DICOM-rs feature adapters for normal generation. External subprocess tools require explicit feature gating and version reporting.
policy_decisions.rationale: The generator must remain deterministic, portable, and reportable. Subprocess tools can be useful for codecs with no mature Rust path, but they add deployment and reproducibility risk.
policy_decisions.next_action: Design the Phase 1 codec trait so both in-process adapters and explicit external backends can report identity, options, feature gates, and determinism.

policy_decisions.recommendation: Default-supported codec backends must be permissively licensed or already compatible with the repository license. GPL or AGPL tooling is deferred to optional local experiments unless explicitly approved later.
policy_decisions.rationale: Generated corpus support should be usable in CI and downstream viewer projects without creating redistribution ambiguity.
policy_decisions.next_action: Record license evidence before moving any external backend from research_more to implement_now.

policy_decisions.recommendation: Implement RLE Lossless first, then verify existing DICOM-rs feature adapters for JPEG Baseline, JPEG-LS, and JPEG XL before selecting external-heavy JPEG 2000 or HTJ2K paths.
policy_decisions.rationale: RLE is bounded, lossless, and suitable for proving the generator-owned encapsulated pixel data loop before adding heavyweight codec dependencies.
policy_decisions.next_action: Start Phase 1 with the minimal codec adapter API needed by a native RLE encoder.

validation_strategy: Unit-test segment ordering and byte-run packet boundaries.
Round-trip tiny generated frames through the DICOM-rs RLE decoder when the rle feature is enabled.
Validate encapsulated Pixel Data structure and decoded frame hashes in the generated manifest.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs exposes RLE Lossless decode support behind the rle feature and no pixel-data writer.

codec_families.next_action: Add a minimal codec adapter trait and native RLE frame encoder without flipping the skipped registry row until generation, validation, reporting, and reproducibility all pass.

validation_strategy: Generate a tiny RGB Secondary Capture frame through the DICOM-rs JPEG Baseline writer when the project jpeg feature is enabled.
Decode the generated codestream through the DICOM-rs JPEG Baseline reader and enforce a bounded per-sample tolerance.
Record lossy image compression metadata and semantic-stable determinism in the manifest.
blockers: Lossy encoder byte stability is not assumed; generated cases remain semantic-stable.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs provides JPEG Baseline pixel-data reader and writer adapters when built with the jpeg feature.

codec_families.next_action: Keep the first JPEG Baseline case feature-gated and expand only after generated output, validation, reports, and reproducibility remain stable.

validation_strategy: Generate a tiny monochrome Secondary Capture frame through the pinned CharLS-backed DICOM-rs JPEG-LS Lossless writer when the project charls feature is enabled.
Require exact decoded hashes for JPEG-LS Lossless.
Record CharLS version and build mode in generated manifests.

required_before_implementation: Choose the first near-lossless error limit and pixel shape.
Define expected decoded-frame tolerance and visual semantics.
Set Lossy Image Compression, Lossy Image Compression Ratio, and Lossy Image Compression Method metadata policy.
Prove DICOM-rs CharLS near-lossless encode/decode behavior and reproducibility under the project charls feature.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs has CharLS-backed JPEG-LS pixel-data writer code behind the charls feature.
The project charls feature exposes a DICOM-rs JPEG-LS Lossless writer and reader that round-trip a tiny 8-bit MONOCHROME2 frame exactly.

codec_families.next_action: Proceed to JPEG XL lossless feature verification before adding any JPEG-LS Near-Lossless generated case.

validation_strategy: Use the project jpegxl feature to expose pinned DICOM-rs JPEG XL Lossless writer and reader adapters.
Require decoded frame hash validation and backend version reporting.
Classify lossy JPEG XL separately after lossless support is proven.
blockers: Lossy JPEG XL policy is not decided.

lossy_policy.defer_reason: Lossy JPEG XL needs explicit lossy Image Pixel metadata, decoded tolerance validation, and reproducibility policy before a generated conformance case is added.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs has JPEG XL decode support through jxl-oxide and lossless encode support through zune-jpegxl behind its jpegxl feature.

The project jpegxl feature exposes a DICOM-rs JPEG XL Lossless writer and reader that round-trip a tiny 8-bit RGB frame exactly, with backend metadata reporting jxl-oxide 0.10.2 and zune-jpegxl 0.4.0.
The feature-gated JPEG XL Lossless Secondary Capture case generates encapsulated Pixel Data and validates exact decoded frame hashes during generation and CLI validation.

lossy_policy.defer_reason: Lossy JPEG 2000 needs explicit lossy Image Pixel metadata, decoded tolerance validation, and reproducibility policy before a generated conformance case is added.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs exposes JPEG 2000 decoding behind openjp2/openjpeg-sys feature flags and uses NeverPixelAdapter for encoding, so this project needs its own writer wrapper.
The local pinned jpeg2k crate exposes OpenJPEG-backed save_as_file_with and from_bytes APIs; the first project spike should prove an in-process lossless J2K codestream path before generation.
The selected first backend uses the BSD-2-Clause pure Rust openjp2 crate instead of a system OpenJPEG subprocess or native C build path.
The project jpeg2000 feature exposes a project-owned OpenJPEG-rs writer plus DICOM-rs reader validation that round-trips a tiny 16-bit MONOCHROME2 frame exactly.
The generated Secondary Capture JPEG 2000 Lossless case uses encapsulated Pixel Data and validates exact decoded frame hashes during generation and CLI validation.

codec_families.next_action: Keep JPEG 2000 lossy deferred until lossy semantics are selected; choose the next Phase 4 target by either researching HTJ2K backend viability or selecting an independent JPEG 2000 validator for expanded coverage.

integration_mode.version_discovery: The local `ojph_compress` binary rejects `-v`, `-h`, and `--help`; the project wrapper therefore reports the resolved executable path and SHA-256 executable fingerprint as the portable backend identity until a reliable version command is available.
integration_mode.fingerprint_strategy: Resolve `ojph_compress` through PATH or an explicit command path, canonicalize the executable path, and record the SHA-256 of the executable bytes with the fixed encoder options.
integration_mode.input_path: Use 16-bit MONOCHROME2 PGM input with big-endian sample bytes and `-num_decomps 1` for the first proof-backed OpenJPH HTJ2K Lossless path. Do not use the raw/YUV path with `-num_decomps 0`; it failed edge-domain unsigned 16-bit round-trip checks.
integration_mode.policy: Invoke OpenJPH only through an explicit project wrapper that discovers the tool, records the executable version or executable fingerprint when available plus fixed encoder options, and reports the external backend in manifests. Do not vendor OpenJPH C++ or add an FFI wrapper for the first generated case.

validation_strategy: OpenJPH can encode a tiny 16-bit unsigned MONOCHROME2 PGM frame into an HTJ2K Lossless codestream that the DICOM-rs OpenJPEG-backed HTJ2K reader decodes exactly for sampled edge-domain values including zero and high unsigned samples.
Integrate OpenJPH as an explicit external command wrapper for the first generated case, not as a vendored C++ build or FFI wrapper.
Use DICOM-rs OpenJPEG-backed HTJ2K decode support as the first independent reader and compare exact native frame hashes in generation and CLI validation.
Record the OpenJPH executable path and executable SHA-256 fingerprint because this local binary does not expose a working version command.
Defer RPCL and lossy HTJ2K variants until lossless support is proven.
blockers: OpenJPH semantic identity currently depends on executable SHA-256 fingerprinting because the local `ojph_compress` binary does not expose a working `-v`, `-h`, or `--help` version command.
No mature Rust-native HTJ2K encoder dependency is pinned in this project.
Grok has HTJ2K support but is AGPL v3, so it is excluded from default generation by the project licensing policy.

candidate_backends.name: OpenJPH
candidate_backends.rationale: OpenJPH targets HTJ2K directly and has a permissive license that fits the default backend policy. A local external-command spike proved exact DICOM-rs decode for a tiny 16-bit unsigned MONOCHROME2 PGM frame with edge-domain sample values. The first project integration should preserve that proven path as a discoverable external command rather than adding vendored C++ or FFI scope.

candidate_backends.name: Grok
candidate_backends.rationale: Grok documents HTJ2K support and broad platform coverage, but its AGPL v3 license conflicts with the default backend licensing policy. Keep it out of normal generation unless a later explicit optional-tool policy approves it.

candidate_backends.name: Rust-native or Rust FFI crate
candidate_backends.rationale: No OpenJPH, Grok, or HTJ2K encoder crate is present in the pinned project dependencies or local Cargo registry snapshot. A crates.io search could not be completed in the sandbox, so this remains a research item before implementation.

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs exposes HTJ2K Lossless as a decoder implementation behind the openjp2/openjpeg-sys feature flags and otherwise as a stub descriptor; writer support remains unavailable.
OpenJPH describes itself as an open-source HTJ2K implementation and reports a BSD-2-Clause license.
Grok documents HTJ2K support and Rust bindings, but states that it is licensed under AGPL v3.

No OpenJPH, Grok, or HTJ2K encoder dependency is pinned locally. `cargo search htj2k` could not be completed because crates.io DNS resolution is unavailable in the sandbox and escalation was rejected.

OpenJPH produced a raw HTJ2K codestream with SOC/EOC markers from a 16-bit MONOCHROME2 PGM input that DICOM-rs 0.9.1 decoded through the HTJ2K Lossless transfer syntax with exact native bytes for a tiny 2x4 unsigned frame including zero, midrange, and high unsigned values.

Running the selected PGM-input `ojph_compress` command twice for the same tiny edge-domain unsigned 16-bit MONOCHROME2 frame produced byte-identical HTJ2K codestream hashes, so command-level byte reproducibility is proven for the sampled first-case domain.

The earlier raw/YUV input path with `-num_decomps 0` did not round-trip the broader unsigned 16-bit sample domain through the pinned DICOM-rs HTJ2K reader; the selected PGM path with `-num_decomps 1` resolves that sample interpretation issue for the first 16-bit MONOCHROME2 case.

The first HTJ2K integration mode is an explicit OpenJPH external-command wrapper so the project can reuse the proven command-line path while keeping vendored C++ and FFI work out of the initial generation slice.

The project `htj2k_openjph` feature exposes an OpenJPH external-command wrapper that resolves `ojph_compress`, fingerprints the executable with SHA-256, encodes fixed-option PGM input, validates SOC/EOC markers, and decodes the resulting HTJ2K Lossless codestream through the pinned DICOM-rs OpenJPEG-backed reader.

The first feature-gated generated HTJ2K Lossless Secondary Capture case records OpenJPH executable SHA-256 runtime identity metadata and validates exact decoded native frame hashes during generation and CLI validation.

codec_families.next_action: Keep HTJ2K lossy and RPCL variants deferred until lossy semantics, encoder options, and validation policy are selected; choose the next Phase 5 legacy/specialty compressed syntax research target.

integration_mode.reason: DCMTK documents DICOM-level JPEG encoding for the legacy transfer syntaxes; local spikes proved metadata preservation, deterministic UID behavior, fragment layout control, DICOM-rs decode validation, and local byte-identical reproducibility for JPEG Lossless SV1 and JPEG Lossless Process 14 sources; and the project now has feature-gated generated SV1 and Process 14 cases that capture runtime identity, validate exact decoded native frame hashes, and report corpus coverage.

validation_strategy: Generate a deterministic uncompressed Secondary Capture source in a temporary file, compress it through the feature-gated dcmcjpeg wrapper, then keep only the compressed JPEG Lossless SV1 or JPEG Lossless Process 14 Part 10 file in the corpus.
Compare decoded native frame hashes against the source frame through the pinned DICOM-rs JPEG decoder and verify encapsulated Pixel Data, Basic Offset Table, and one-fragment frame semantics.
Record the dcmcjpeg command, canonical executable path, executable SHA-256, version banner, and fixed encoder options in the generated manifest.
Use semantic-stable determinism for the generated case because the external tool identity is manifest-recorded even though local repeated outputs are byte-identical.
Treat JPEG Extended 12-bit as a separate feature gate once the process is proven.

evidence.query: lookup_uid JPEGExtended12Bit; lookup_uid JPEGLossless; lookup_uid JPEGLosslessSV1

evidence.finding: Pinned DICOM-rs JPEG feature descriptors create legacy JPEG transfer syntax values with encoder=false for JPEG Extended 12-bit, JPEG Lossless Process 14, and JPEG Lossless SV1.
Pinned DICOM-rs 0.9.1 documents JPEG Extended and JPEG Lossless transfer syntaxes as decode-capable under the jpeg feature but without encoding support.

DCMTK dcmcjpeg documents DICOM file compression to JPEG transfer syntaxes, including options for JPEG Lossless SV1, JPEG Lossless Process 14, JPEG Extended, true-lossless mode, one-fragment-per-frame output, Basic Offset Table creation, and UID preservation.
DCMTK dcmjpeg documents library-level codec registration for converting between uncompressed and JPEG-compressed DICOM representations, including a lossless JPEG SV1 example.
DCMTK documents BSD-style redistribution terms for the toolkit and includes an adapted IJG JPEG toolkit notice for dcmjpeg.

evidence.query: command -v dcmcjpeg; command -v gdcmconv; command -v cjpeg
evidence.finding: DCMTK dcmcjpeg is available after installing Homebrew dcmtk 3.7.0; gdcmconv remains unavailable and /opt/homebrew/bin/cjpeg is still not selected because it is not DICOM-aware.

DCMTK dcmcjpeg compressed the deterministic classic/sc/mono2_u16_explicit_le source to JPEG Lossless SV1 with --encode-lossless-sv1 and to JPEG Lossless Process 14 with --encode-lossless, both using --true-lossless, --fragment-per-frame, --offset-table-create, and --uid-never; both outputs preserved SOP Class UID, SOP Instance UID, Synthetic Data, and Patient ID, used one Basic Offset Table entry and one fragment, decoded exactly through the pinned DICOM-rs JPEG Lossless readers, and repeated byte-identically for the same source and options.

The project legacy_jpeg_dcmtk feature exposes a DCMTK dcmcjpeg file-level wrapper for JPEG Lossless SV1 and JPEG Lossless Process 14 that records the canonical executable path, executable SHA-256, and version banner at runtime while preserving source metadata and exact decoded native frame bytes.
